title: Zodiac
synopsis: San Francisco, late seventies. You're the kid in the newsroom who can't stop staring at the killer's ciphers. Your boss doesn't think it's your job. He's wrong.

nodes.text: It arrives at the paper in a manila envelope. The cipher is in three colors. You are, technically, the political cartoonist.

choices.consequence: There is no taking “Look at it anyway” back. Curious shapes the silence before the next moment arrives.
The decision settles the question for now. Its verdict—Discipline—follows you into whatever comes next.

nodes.text: Inspector Toschi, on the phone, is polite and brittle. He has many cases. This is one.

choices.consequence: The choice lands, and the scene changes around it. If it has a name, that name is Volunteer.
There is no taking “Stay out of his way” back. Respect shapes the silence before the next moment arrives.

nodes.text: Your editor laughs. He tells you to stick to cartoons. You realize, slowly, that he is also curious.

choices.consequence: You let the choice stand. The path shifts almost imperceptibly, marked by one lasting impulse: Push.
The choice lands, and the scene changes around it. If it has a name, that name is Stealth.

nodes.text: On weekends you visit, on your own dime, every public crime scene. None of them tell you anything you didn't already read.

choices.consequence: You let the choice stand. The path shifts almost imperceptibly, marked by one lasting impulse: Discipline.
You let the choice stand. The path shifts almost imperceptibly, marked by one lasting impulse: Pragmatic.

nodes.text: The reporter assigned to the case, Avery, is at the bar. He is, by 8 p.m., drunker than you are. He is also smarter.

choices.consequence: You commit to “Drink with him.” The story records the instinct as “Source” and carries it forward.
The choice lands, and the scene changes around it. If it has a name, that name is Friend.

nodes.text: A teacher and his wife crack one of the ciphers in their kitchen. The cipher is, on cracking, mostly Christian theology and ego.

choices.consequence: You commit to “Use the cipher's tells.” The story records the instinct as “Read” and carries it forward.
“Pass it up the chain” closes one possibility and opens another. The moment leaves a clear note behind: Process.

nodes.text: Your wife wants to know why you're not home. You realize you don't have a good answer that isn't, slowly, ruining you.

choices.text: Tell her the obsession is the thing
choices.consequence: You commit to “Tell her the obsession is the thing.” The story records the instinct as “Honest” and carries it forward.
You commit to “Promise to come home earlier.” The story records the instinct as “Promise” and carries it forward.

nodes.text: Avery hands you a manila folder. He is, he says, done with it. He is leaving the paper.

choices.consequence: There is no taking “Take the folder” back. Pick up shapes the silence before the next moment arrives.
There is no taking “Refuse it” back. Honor shapes the silence before the next moment arrives.

nodes.text: A man named Allen, school employee, lake area, the right kind of wrong. You read his file three nights in a row.

choices.consequence: There is no taking “Stay on Allen” back. Long shapes the silence before the next moment arrives.
You let the choice stand. The path shifts almost imperceptibly, marked by one lasting impulse: Open.

nodes.text: Toschi has been re-investigated by his own department after a forged letter. He is, professionally, dying.

choices.consequence: The decision settles the question for now. Its verdict—Friend—follows you into whatever comes next.
The decision settles the question for now. Its verdict—Reporter—follows you into whatever comes next.

nodes.text: Your editor finally lets you write. The article is, by his hand, half its original length. It is still, in places, accurate.

choices.consequence: “Run the article” closes one possibility and opens another. The moment leaves a clear note behind: Print.
The choice lands, and the scene changes around it. If it has a name, that name is Patient.

nodes.text: You notice, one night, that you are being followed. You don't know by whom. The follower, you suspect, is your own paranoia.

choices.consequence: The decision settles the question for now. Its verdict—Discipline—follows you into whatever comes next.
“Confront” closes one possibility and opens another. The moment leaves a clear note behind: Stupid.

nodes.text: You visit Allen's trailer with your editor's permission. He is mostly silent. He stares at you for a long minute. You leave with nothing and everything.

choices.consequence: You let the choice stand. The path shifts almost imperceptibly, marked by one lasting impulse: Instinct.
You commit to “Trust the evidence.” The story records the instinct as “Process” and carries it forward.

nodes.text: Allen takes a polygraph. The polygraph says, ambiguously, no. You realize polygraphs say ambiguously, no.

choices.consequence: You commit to “Use the result anyway.” The story records the instinct as “Selective” and carries it forward.
There is no taking “Drop the angle” back. Honest shapes the silence before the next moment arrives.

nodes.text: Your daughter, six, asks why you are not at her recital. You sit her on your knee that night and tell her, almost, the truth.

choices.text: Promise to be at the next one
choices.consequence: The decision settles the question for now. Its verdict—Vow—follows you into whatever comes next.

choices.text: Promise to step back from the case
choices.consequence: You let the choice stand. The path shifts almost imperceptibly, marked by one lasting impulse: Bigger vow.

nodes.text: You get, by way of a sympathetic clerk, copies of files you should not, technically, have. They contain, finally, the thing nobody has named.

choices.consequence: The decision settles the question for now. Its verdict—Discreet—follows you into whatever comes next.
You commit to “Don't use them.” The story records the instinct as “Honor” and carries it forward.

nodes.text: Toschi retires. He invites you to his backyard party. You go. He thanks you for the company more than the help.

choices.consequence: “Stay in touch” closes one possibility and opens another. The moment leaves a clear note behind: Friend.
The choice lands, and the scene changes around it. If it has a name, that name is Boundary.

nodes.text: You decide to write a book. The book is a years-long project. The book is, you realize, your only path to closure.

choices.consequence: The decision settles the question for now. Its verdict—Years—follows you into whatever comes next.
The choice lands, and the scene changes around it. If it has a name, that name is Pilot.

nodes.text: The manuscript is, in the end, careful and damning. It accuses Allen by implication. Your lawyer goes through every page twice.

choices.consequence: You commit to “Publish.” The story records the instinct as “Risk” and carries it forward.
“Publish a less specific version” closes one possibility and opens another. The moment leaves a clear note behind: Discipline.

nodes.text: A letter from a woman who survived a Zodiac attack, decades ago. She thanks you. She also, in passing, names the man you suspected.

choices.text: Take her letter at face value
choices.consequence: You let the choice stand. The path shifts almost imperceptibly, marked by one lasting impulse: Trust.
You commit to “Verify with her police report.” The story records the instinct as “Verify” and carries it forward.

nodes.text: You are old now. The case is, technically, unsolved. You are, technically, retired. You realize 'unsolved' is not the same as 'unknown.'

choices.consequence: “Stay quietly satisfied” closes one possibility and opens another. The moment leaves a clear note behind: Quiet.
“Take one last lap” closes one possibility and opens another. The moment leaves a clear note behind: Loud.
Some endings reveal themselves last.

nodes.text: The book becomes the definitive account. Other writers use it. A film is, eventually, made from it. You are credited as a consultant. You attend the premiere. You are bored. You are, also, grateful.
You go back to cartoons. You discover, late, that you are good at them. You publish a small collection of newsroom-life cartoons that does, surprisingly, well. Your daughter laughs at every one.
In your eighties you receive, in your mail, an envelope with a cipher in three colors. You do not, this time, open it for the paper. You open it for yourself.
